title: Молодуха Лепса поставила на место накинувшегося на нее Киркорова
description: <p>В эфире популярного шоу "Мастер игры"  произошел инцидент, который не оставил зрителей равнодушными. Аврора Киба, молодая невеста Григория Лепса, стала объектом нападок со стороны Филиппа Киркорова. </p><p>Вчерашняя школьница не раз сталкивалась с критикой из-за романа с 62-летним певцом. В эфире шоу не удалось избежать острой темы, и у девушки стали допытываться, для чего ей нужны отношения с человеком, который на 40 лет старше. Киба дала понять, что ей не хочется обсуждать отношения с певцом, однако под натиском Филиппа Киркорова сдалась.</p><p>"Почему вы не можете ответить? Ответьте еще раз, если вас спрашивают", &#8212; возмутился Филипп. "Мое тело &#8212; мое дело. Какие еще вопросы?" &#8212; эмоционально ответила Аврора. Молодуха Лепса не только не испугалась, но и поставила на место поп-короля, защитив свою личность и личную жизнь.</p><p>Это не первая стычка с поп-королем. Ранее Филипп Киркоров отметил, что не понимает, для чего Аврора Киба участвует в шоу "Мастер игры", ведь она просто чья-то невеста. Девушка не согласилась с такой оценкой, подчеркнув, что получает образование в одном из лучших учебных заведений мира, а Лепс просил ее руки четыре раза. Позднее Аврора Киба подчеркнула, что не чувствует неприязни со стороны популярного артиста. </p>

title: Бывший зек Ефремов упал в ноги Михалкову на глазах Собчак
description: <p>В июне 2020 года жизнь Михаила Ефремова кардинально изменилась. Артист в состоянии алкогольного и наркотического опьянения нарушил правила дорожного движения и столкнулся с фургоном, водитель которого скоропостижно скончался. </p><p>Суд приговорил Ефремова к 7,5 годам колонии общего режима. Пару месяцев назад актер вышел на свободу, адвокатам удалось добиться условно-досрочного освобождения. Всего в колонии артист провел около 4,5 лет. </p><p>По возвращении домой Михаил Ефремов, судя по всему, захотел восстановить работу по профессии. Чтобы процесс пошел быстрее, бывший зек решил упасть в ноги Никите Михалкову и написал режиссеру трогательное письмо с просьбой принять его на работу. </p><p>Как оказалось, эта сцена произошла на глазах у Ксении Собчак. Она подтвердила информацию о возвращении Михаила Ефремова на сцену:</p><p class="article__quote">"Все так, действительно, Никита Сергеевич помог, я &#8212; свидетель. Миша написал письмо, и оно Михалкова тронуло."</p><p>Некоторые убеждены, что режиссер помог Ефремову с восстановлением карьеры, но и содействовал досрочному освобождению. Скоро актер появится на сцене театра "Мастерской 12", которым руководит Никита Сергеевич. </p><p>Напомним, в начале июня снова появились слухи о романе 61-летнего Ефремова с 42-летней коллегой Дарьей Белоусовой. После злосчастного ДТП, судя по всему, актер отсиживался у любовницы, а позднее она регулярно навещала его в тюрьме. Правда, не совсем понятно, что об отношениях артиста думает его жена. Михаил Ефремов все еще состоит в официальном браке с Софьей Кругликовой. </p>

title: Потерявшая ребенка Муцениеце торопится в ЗАГС после слухов о новой беременности
description: <p>После болезненного развода с Павлом Прилучным Агата Муцениеце пережила немало потрясений. Актриса активно строила карьеру, играла в театре и, казалось, обрела счастье в отношениях с музыкантом Петром Дрангой. </p><p>Однако недавнее решение сына Тимофея переехать к отцу стало для Агаты настоящим ударом &#8211; мальчик отказывается общаться с мамой и даже с младшей сестрой Мией. Впрочем, похоже, потерявшая ребенка, точнее контакт с ним, актриса нашла силы двигаться дальше.</p><p>В конце весны Дранга сделал Муцениеце предложение, и она ответила согласием. По слухам, пара планирует сыграть свадьбу уже в июле. </p><p class="article__quote">"Свадьба будет в июле &#8211; это точно", поделился продюсер Сергей Дворцов.</p><p>Он сообщил, что церемония пройдет за границей, а официальная часть &#8211; в Москве. Возможно, это связано с тем, что Агата Муцениеце из Латвии, там до сих пор живет ее семья, и актриса хочет зарегистрировать брак на родине. </p><p>Многие связывают скорую свадьбу с интересным положением звезды &#8211; по слухам, у актрисы случилась новая беременность, и она ждет третьего ребенка. В последнее время Муцениеце действительно стала реже появляться на публике, а ее фигура, по мнению поклонников, заметно округлилась. Недоброжелатели утверждают, что отцом будущего ребенка может быть вовсе не Петр Дранга, а таинственный богатый поклонник, о котором судачили в светской тусовке.</p><p>Напомним, развод Агаты Муцениеце и Павла Прилучного сопровождался громким скандалом. Актриса обвиняла бывшего супруга в домашнем насилии и изменах. После расставания экс-супруги долгое время не могли наладить отношения, причиной споров были алименты. Теперь же яблоком раздора стал их старший сын Тимофей, который решил жить с отцом и его новой женой Зепюр Брутян.</p><p><script async src="https://telegram.org/js/telegram-widget.js?22" data-telegram-post="dnishowbiz/12954" data-width="100%"></script></p>

title: Сбежавшая от мужа Саша Савельева столкнулась с новым предательством
description: <p>"Я просто хочу защищать свой труд!" &#8211; в отчаянии говорит певица в видео, которое опубликовала в своих соцсетях. По словам звезды, она уже несколько месяцев переносит релиз своих песен, так как не может получить готовый материал от звукорежиссера.</p><p>Саша Савельева, сбежавшая от мужа в Москву по рабочим вопросам, столкнулась с новым предательством. По словам певицы, она долго работала над новым треком, песня была записана на двух языках и должна была стать хитом, но звукорежиссер, имя которого пока не называется, просто пропал.</p><p class="article__quote">"Звукорежиссер, с которым я работала, просто исчез и не отвечает ни мне, ни людям, с которыми я работаю", &#8211; пожаловалась Савельева.</p><p>Певица призналась, что долго закрывала глаза на срывы со стороны необязательного коллеги, надеясь сохранить хорошие отношения, но ее лояльность не оправдалась. В итоге Савельева дала звукорежиссеру три дня на исправление ситуации. Она пригрозила, что если в течение этого времени он не выйдет на связь и не передаст весь материал, она озвучит его имя.</p><p>Ситуация осложняется тем, что Саша Савельева работала со звукорежиссером без официального договора. Это означает, что привлечь его к юридической ответственности будет крайне сложно.</p><p><script async src="https://telegram.org/js/telegram-widget.js?22" data-telegram-post="dnishowbiz/13429" data-width="100%"></script></p><p>История Саши Савельевой вызвала широкий отклик в социальных сетях. Поклонники выражают свою поддержку певице и надеются на скорейшее разрешение конфликта. Особое внимание привлекла реакция продюсера Иосифа Пригожина, который предложил коллеге помощь в решении проблемы.</p><p>Однако Саша Савельева, несмотря на трудности, не теряет надежды на лучшее. Она продолжает работать над новыми проектами и верит, что справедливость восторжествует.</p>

title: Молодежный экофестиваль состоялся в Петербурге на полях НМЭК
description: <p>Санкт-Петербург стал центром притяжения молодых экоактивистов и экспертов: 21 мая здесь прошел масштабный Молодежный экофестиваль &#171;Росатом Экофест&#187;. Событие собрало свыше 500 участников и представило десятки волонтерских и экологических проектов и инициатив. У гостей также была возможность познакомиться с деятельностью и карьерными траекториями в Госкорпорации &#171;Росатом&#187;.</p><p><img src="https://img.dni.ru/binaries/v3_addition_to_material/1879435.jpg" width="585" height="390"     alt="Фото: пресс-служба"></p><p>Фестиваль стал преддверием и частью программы XI Невского международного экологического конгресса (НМЭК), который запланирован на 22-23 мая в Таврическом дворце. Проведение экофестиваля было поддержано Госкорпорацией &#171;Росатом&#187;, а в числе его партнеров выступили Всероссийское экологическое общественное движение &#171;Экосистема&#187; и Федеральное агентство по делам молодёжи (Росмолодежь). Сам Конгресс организуют Правительство РФ, Совет Федерации, Межпарламентская Ассамблея стран СНГ и Минприроды России при операторской поддержке Фонда Росконгресс.</p><p><img src="https://img.dni.ru/binaries/v3_addition_to_material/1879436.jpg" width="585" height="390"     alt="Фото: пресс-служба"></p><p>На площадке фестиваля собрались профессионалы и энтузиасты экологической сферы: от экопредпринимателей и экспертов в области экотехнологий, ответственного потребления и практической экологии, до активистов, волонтеров и студентов ведущих петербургских вузов.</p><p>С приветственным словом к собравшимся обратилась Татьяна Терентьева, заместитель генерального директора по персоналу Госкорпорации &#171;Росатом&#187;. Она подчеркнула, что главная цель этого уже второго молодежного дня на полях НМЭК &#8211; вдохновить талантливую молодежь на создание новых, прорывных решений в области экологии, а также на вдумчивое осмысление влияния их будущей работы и повседневной жизни на окружающую среду. По ее словам, экологическая трансформация немыслима без участия молодых людей &#8211; без их идей и готовности не просто заботиться о природе, но и формировать новую экономическую модель, новые подходы и даже новые профессии. Татьяна Терентьева выразила уверенность, что именно нынешнее поколение станет теми лидерами, которые изменят парадигму устойчивого развития, и отметила, что Росатом, являясь мировым лидером в сфере зеленой энергетики, готов оказывать им всяческую поддержку.</p><p><img src="https://img.dni.ru/binaries/v3_addition_to_material/1879437.jpg" width="585" height="390"     alt="Фото: пресс-служба"></p><p>В работе фестиваля приняли участие и пообщались с гостями видные деятели отрасли и представители власти, включая директора направления по реализации госпрограмм в сфере экологии Росатома Андрея Лебедева, заместителя губернатора Нижегородской области Олега Берковича, директора проектного офиса по внутренним коммуникациям и КСО Росатома Анну Жигульскую, советника руководителя Росмолодёжи Олега Макарова, а также сопредседателей Движения &#171;Экосистема&#187; Александру Рябых и Андрея Руднева (он же председатель ВОД &#171;Делай!&#187;).</p><p>О ключевых направлениях деятельности Росатома в области экологии рассказал Андрей Лебедев. Он отметил, что Госкорпорация активно развивает новые бизнес-векторы, особенно связанные с обращением с отходами и ликвидацией накопленного экологического ущерба. Лебедев подчеркнул востребованность российских компетенций на международной арене, указав на расширение партнерства со странами СНГ и другими государствами, где растет запрос на безопасные и эффективные решения. Он привел примеры уже реализуемых масштабных проектов, таких как рекультивация промплощадки в Усолье-Сибирском, очистка территорий Байкальского ЦБК и полигона &#8220;Красный Бор&#8221;. По словам Лебедева, это не просто природоохранные инициативы, а фундаментальная работа, закладывающая основу для устойчивого развития и перехода к экономике замкнутого цикла.</p><p>Важной частью программы стала презентация карьерных перспектив в Госкорпорации &#171;Росатом&#187; для молодых специалистов. Были представлены вакансии для инженеров-экологов, экспертов по устойчивому развитию, IT-специалистов, энергетиков и проектировщиков.</p><p>На фестивале нашлось место и для конкретных экологических действий и полезных активностей. В рамках совместного проекта &#171;Редкое совпадение&#187; Росатома и ФМБА России более 50 посетителей смогли стать потенциальными донорами костного мозга, вступив в Федеральный регистр. Также петербуржцы участвовали в мастер-классах по апсайклингу (созданию новых вещей из старых), сдавали на переработку определенные виды отходов прямо на площадке и углубляли свои знания о правилах раздельного сбора мусора.</p><p>Образовательный блок фестиваля включал лекции от ведущих экоэкспертов. Руководитель пресс-службы Федерального экологического оператора (ФЭО) Антонина Громова продемонстрировала, как опасные отходы I и II классов могут быть не только обезврежены, но и стать ресурсом для создания новых пространств &#8211; зон отдыха, спортивных объектов или туристических маршрутов. Роман Саблин, признанный первым экотренером в России и СНГ и основатель компании &#171;Зеленый Драйвер&#187;, поделился практическими советами по внедрению экологичных привычек в повседневную жизнь. А сооснователь экоцентра &#171;Сборка&#187; Сергей Тушев рассказал о своем опыте запуска экопроекта &#8220;с нуля&#8221; и объяснил, почему бизнесу выгоден раздельный сбор отходов.</p><p>Культурная программа также была насыщена: в рамках первой в мире Международной биеннале экологического искусства посетители смогли эксклюзивно увидеть экспонаты выставки &#171;Чистая энергия&#187;, представляющие художественное видение различных видов энергии &#8211; звуковой, электрической и атомной. На территории портовой зоны, где проходил фестиваль, также экспонировались фотоработы, запечатлевшие животный мир регионов присутствия атомной отрасли, как часть федеральной выставки &#171;Первозданная Россия&#187;.</p><p>Для тех, кто предпочитает активный отдых, была организована возможность попробовать себя в яхтенном спорте: под наставничеством профессиональных инструкторов участники выходили в акваторию Финского залива, осваивая азы управления парусами.</p><p>Завершился Молодежный экофестиваль ярким финалом. Гостей ждал модный показ от проекта &#171;Бережно&#187;, ставшего победителем &#171;Экоакселератора Росатома&#187;. Коллекция была полностью создана из переработанных материалов, а представленные образы включали отсылки к элементам национальных костюмов. Праздник завершился диджей-сетом на живописном фоне Финского залива, а также розыгрышами ценных призов, включая поездки в атомные города в рамках &#171;Тура возможностей&#187;.</p>

title: Embraced across divides, Dolly Parton leaves a lasting legacy
description: Throughout her lifetime, Dolly Parton worked to build a better world, while becoming inextricable from the American imagination. She was embraced by fans across gender, race and class, embodying a mythology typically inaccessible to even the most influential historical figures. It is one of her greatest legacies: to take what you have and help someone with it.

title: Trump scores much-needed double primary victory in South Carolina, Oklahoma
description: US President Donald Trump scored two badly needed victories Tuesday as his preferred candidates in South Carolina and Oklahoma won the Republican runoffs. The sweep interrupts a bruising run for Trump, whose endorsed candidates had lost 10 Republican contests this cycle, including six in the previous two weeks, as his own approval ratings fell sharply.

title: Fire at maternity ward in Islamabad hospital kills 14 infants
description: A dawn fire that erupted in the maternity ward of Islamabad's premier public hospital, Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), on Wednesday killed 14 infants, Pakistan authorities said, blaming a faulty air conditioner for the blaze. Witnesses described harrowing scenes and a slow response from emergency services and guards reportedly preventing them from leaving the ward.

title: Premier League: Cameroon's Carlos Baleba transferred to Manchester United
description: Cameroonian midfielder Carlos Baleba has moved from Brighton to Manchester United for around €75 million.

title: Middle East live: Iran says Hormuz strait still closed despite transit corridor talks with Oman
description: Tehran warned on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed unless the United States ends the war, despite discussions with Oman on a temporary transit corridor in the vital waterway. Washington had earlier announced fresh sanctions aimed at pressuring Iran to capitulate, with US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent threatening the country with "economic asphyxiation". Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

title: Iceland to vote on reopening EU membership talks in close referendum
description: Icelanders will vote in a referendum on Saturday whether to resume entry talks with the European Union amid growing global insecurity. Voters are not being asked to decide just yet if they want to join the 27-member bloc – only whether they want their government to negotiate possible terms.

title: Trump sends Saudi civil nuclear agreement to Congress for review
description: US President Donald Trump has submitted a civilian nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress for review, an administration official said. The classified pact, sent to Capitol Hill on Monday, is aimed at bolstering Riyadh’s nuclear programme but remains contingent on Saudi Arabia normalising relations with Israel.

title: SpaceX to build $100 billion rocket launch facility in southern Louisiana
description: SpaceX unveiled plans on Tuesday for a $100 billion rocket launch complex in southern Louisiana, its largest yet, aimed at supporting Starship and AI satellite missions. The 125,000-acre Starbase Louisiana site on Pecan Island could eventually handle thousands of Starship launches annually, the company said.

title: Oil prices fall for second day as US shifts from Iran strikes to sanctions
description: Oil prices fell for a second straight day on Tuesday as traders saw a reduced risk of renewed US military strikes on Iran after Washington instead threatened broader economic sanctions. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent declared an “economic D-Day” against Tehran but gave no timeline or details on countries that could face penalties.

title: US-led Gaza peace board warns Hamas over kites after Israeli threat
description: The US-led board overseeing the Gaza peace plan warned Hamas on Tuesday to halt militant activity, including flying kites, after Israel threatened retaliatory strikes. A Board of Peace official said Israel must also respect the ceasefire, limiting military action to responses to “genuine and imminent threats.”

title: Mawlid festivities cancelled in Tigray over drone attacks
description: In tonight's programme: Muslims celebrate Mawlid across Africa but festivities are cancelled in Tigray because of recent drone attacks. But first: the United States calls for beefed-up UN sanctions against the warring parties in Sudan. Finally, in the Kenyan village of Cheporor, a recent discovery of gold sends thousands of amateur prospectors rushing to the area.

title: Syrian Kurdish leader announces SDF dissolution after its integration into army
description: Mazloum Abdi, the commander-in-chief of the Syrian Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) on Tuesday announced the dissolution of the group in a televised speech from the presidential palace in Damascus. The dissolution followed the integration of SDF fighters into the Syrian military, said Abdi, and represented a major victory for Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa.

title: Beloved US country music icon Dolly Parton dies at 80
description: US singer-songwriter, actress, businesswoman and philanthropist Dolly Parton died on Tuesday at the age of 80, her family said in a statement. The prolific songwriter released 49 studio albums, more than 100 compilation and collorabative albums, won 10 Grammys and 13 Academy of Country Music awards, and racked up 26 number one country hits during her six decades in the American music scene.

title: Nigeria’s president orders rescue operation after mass kidnapping at mosque
description: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu on Tuesday ordered security agencies to conduct a rescue operation after the mass kidnapping of worshippers during an attack on a mosque in the north-central Niger State last week. Local authorities were still trying to verify the number of missing people, but local residents said roughly 600 women, children and elderly people had been abducted.

title: Japan: 1,800 people pull 360-tonne Hirosaki Castle keep by hand
description: About 1,800 people came together in northern Japan to pull a 360-tonne castle keep by hand. The Hirosaki Castle keep was moved in 2015 so its earthquake-damaged stone wall could undergo repairs. Now, using hikiya, a technique that places buildings on rollers so they can be moved without dismantling them, the keep is being brought closer to its original position. Those taking part were selected through a lottery system. Moving efforts will continue until the end of August.

title: Cyberattacks target French government agencies
description:
🇫🇷 🧑‍💻 French government agencies are more frequently landing in the crosshairs of hackers, leaving important personal data increasingly vulnerable to cyberattacks.
 
In 2026 alone, organs of the French finance ministry have been victim to three massive cyberattacks, compromising the data of millions of people.
 
FRANCE 24's Tanishk Saha explains what they have revealed - and why you should be concerned.
 
#France #data #cyberattack #finance

title: Canada strikes back at Trump with retaliatory tariffs as US trade war escalates
description: Canada on Tuesday announced retaliatory tariffs on C$27.6 billion ($19.94 billion) worth of US goods, including steel and dairy products, in a dollar-for-dollar response to President Donald Trump's punitive tariffs on Canadian products. Ottawa also announced a C$7.5 billion aid package for impacted Canadian businesses and workers as the trade war between the two countries escalated.

title: French astronaut performs second spacewalk in just a week
description: One week after becoming the first French woman to perform a spacewalk, Sophie Adenot has ventured outside the International Space Station again on August 25 - with the mission of replacing an antenna.

title: Canada's tariffs on US about 'sovereignty to get people on board' with trade war
description: As its trade war with the US deepens, Canada is imposing tariffs on US goods in retaliation for tariffs introduced in the past few days on its goods. Ottawa has also announced a multi-billion aid package for workers and has called on Canadians to buy local to help domestic industries. FRANCE 24's Christopher Guly and Kethevane Gorjestani tell us what to know.

title: Iran offers $10 million to kill Trump's son
description: Iranian state media has aired a video that appears to threaten the life of Barron Trump, US President Donald Trump's youngest son. Since the start of the war in February, Iranian media have on multiple occasions circulated content threatening the president and family members.  The US Secret Service has confirmed it is aware of the video.

title: Replay: Canada announces countermeasures to new US tariffs
description: Rewatch as Canadian ministers lay out a series of countermeasures as its trade war with the US deepens after the Trump administration imposed new tariffs on Canadian goods.

title: France: Tornado ravages small village
description: 🌪️ A tornado of rare intensity devastated the small village of Pomas in southern France, causing widespread destruction and leaving residents in shock on Tuesday, with the mayor describing the aftermath as resembling "wartime". At least 39 people were injured, including two severely.

title: CIA director Ratcliffe visits Moscow, US media reports
description: CIA Director John Ratcliffe ​visited Russia to attend meetings in Moscow on Tuesday, according to two US media outlets, in what is believed to be Ratcliffe's first known trip to Russia since taking over as US spy chief. The reported visit comes as US-brokered talks aimed at ending the Ukraine war have stalled.

Prince Harry quits board of wildlife charity after rangers’ human rights abuses
description: <p>Spokesperson for Duke of Sussex says he remains an ‘active and avid supporter’ of African Parks’ mission</p><p>The Duke of Sussex has stepped down from the board of a major African wildlife charity that had been at the centre of a human rights controversy.</p><p>Prince Harry’s spokesperson confirmed he was no longer a trustee of <a href="https://www.africanparks.org/">African Parks</a>, which <a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq54dgv2p29o">admitted last year </a>that human rights abuses were committed by its rangers in the Republic of the Congo.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/aug/24/prince-harry-quits-board-wildlife-charity-african-parks-human-rights-abuses">Continue reading...</a>

title: Video shows hundreds held captive after Nigeria mosque kidnapping
description: <p>Gunmen ‌attacked worshippers in Dekara village on Friday taking women, children and older people</p><p>An armed group has posted a video showing what ⁠residents said were about ⁠600 women, children and ​older people abducted in an attack on a mosque in Nigeria’s north-central Niger State last week.</p><p>The video, posted on Facebook and WhatsApp, ⁠showed large groups of people seated in a forested area surrounded by armed men. Several children could be heard crying in the background.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/24/video-shows-hundreds-held-captive-after-nigeria-mosque-kidnapping">Continue reading...</a>

title: Children make up half of suspected mpox cases in Guinea-Bissau as epidemic spreads
description: <p>West African country reports 46 suspected cases in outbreak declared in July, amid fears virus may be spreading undetected</p><p>More than half of the mpox cases reported in Guinea-Bissau have been among children, local authorities have said, almost two months since the country announced an epidemic.</p><p>A national outbreak was declared on 4 July, just over a week after a 27-year-old woman became the first confirmed case of mpox in the west African country. Since then, there have been seven confirmed cases and 46 suspected cases. Half of those patients have been children, with 16 under the age of four.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/aug/24/children-half-mpox-disease-cases-guinea-bissau-epidemic-spreads-west-africa">Continue reading...</a>

title: Landslide at waste mound in Guinea capital kills 30, government says
description: <p>Dump site in Conakry, which minister had just promised to move, collapsed after heavy rain in west African state</p><p>A ⁠landslide at a huge waste dump in Guinea’s capital has killed 30 people, the government said on Sunday, after heavy rains overnight prompted it to ⁠collapse, engulfing nearby tents and shacks.</p><p>The incident occurred less than a week after the government announced plans to close the ⁠site and relocate the waste because of the threat it posed, especially during the rainy season, which causes landslides and fatal flash ⁠floods each year in crowded, underdeveloped cities across parts of West Africa.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/23/landslide-waste-mound-conakry-guinea-kills-dozens">Continue reading...</a>

title: US deports 20 people to Liberia, the first of 1,200 migrants under Trump deal
description: <p>Agreement is among largest third-country deportations driven by Trump administration’s immigration crackdown </p><p>Twenty deportees from the United States arrived in Liberia on Thursday, as part of a new agreement that will see the west African country receive as many as 1,200 people under the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/trump-administration">Trump administration</a>’s immigration crackdown.</p><p>The group arrived at the Roberts international airport outside the capital, Monrovia. The Liberia-US agreement is one of the largest third-country deportation arrangements pursued by the administration since Trump returned to office last year.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/20/liberia-deportation-agreement">Continue reading...</a>

title: Wife of US soldier deported after Trump rollback on military family protections
description: <p>Cristy Maryori Villafranca-Trejo, deported to Honduras, is latest military spouse to face removal amid Trump 2.0</p><p>The wife of an active-duty <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/us-military">US soldier</a> was deported on Monday to her native <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/honduras">Honduras</a>, according to her family and the federal Department of Homeland Security (DHS).</p><p>Cristy Maryori Villafranca-Trejo is at least the seventh spouse or parent of an active-duty US soldier to be deported under the immigration crackdown during <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a>’s second presidency.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/25/soldier-wife-deported-honduras">Continue reading...</a>

title: At least 47 killed and dozens kidnapped in gang attack near Haiti capital
description: <p>Gang leader threatens to kill hostages after attack in Kenscoff in which homes were also set alight</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/jul/02/it-was-a-massacre-haiti-gangs-carry-out-mass-killings-across-the-country">‘A massacre’: Haiti gangs carrying out mass killings</a></p></li></ul><p>At least 47 people were killed and more than 50 others kidnapped when armed men attacked a once peaceful community near Haiti’s capital at the weekend, the UN has said.</p><p>A gang leader has threatened to kill the hostages if authorities kill any gang members as they try to secure the community of Kenscoff, nestled in the hills above Port-au-Prince.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/25/gang-attack-kenscoff-port-au-prince-haiti">Continue reading...</a>

title: Supreme court threatens midterms mail-in voting as it backs Trump plan | First Thing
description: <p>US president has been obsessed with restricting the ability to vote by mail, despite using it himself. Plus, why we are still fascinated with Meg from the White Stripes</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/info/2018/sep/17/guardian-us-morning-briefing-sign-up-to-stay-informed">Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here</a></p></li></ul><p>Good morning. The US supreme court has sided with Donald Trump in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/24/supreme-court-trump-mail-in-voting">his effort to crack down on mail-in voting</a>, though it is unclear whether or not his administration will be able to take action before the midterm elections in November. The court’s justices voted 6-3 along ideological lines to lift an injunction that a judge in Massachusetts had placed in June on an executive order issued by the president. But a second injunction remains in place, and the ruling leaves room for legal challenges.</p><p>Trump has repeatedly likened voting by mail to cheating, despite his own use of it and overwhelming evidence that the system is secure. In March he ordered the government to create a “state citizenship list” of eligible voters, requiring that mail-in ballots only be delivered to people on that list. He also directed the justice department to prioritise investigations and prosecutions of state and local election officials who issue ballots to people deemed ineligible to vote in federal elections.</p><p><strong>What did the dissenting judges say?</strong> In a blistering dissent, Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson wrote that the decision “needlessly injects chaos and uncertainty into the upcoming midterm elections”.</p><p><strong>How have rights organisations reacted?</strong> The president of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People, Derrick Johnson, said: “Let this ruling be a reminder that democracy is never, ever guaranteed. We have to fight for it, we have to fight to keep it and we have to protect the rights we do have within it … they are trying to do everything they possibly can to make it difficult for you to vote.”</p><p><strong>How has Canada reacted?</strong> The country’s prime minister, Mark Carney, told reporters that Trump’s announcement was largely expected. “It’s not a surprise for us that the US would take some form of reprisal to our response to their unjustified tariff,” he said. Carney has vowed to match the American tariffs “dollar for dollar”, and said Canada could not accept any proposed trade deal <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/24/canada-trade-deal-trump-mark-carney-french-language">that would weaken French language protections</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/25/first-thing-us-supreme-court-midterms-mail-in-voting-trump-plan">Continue reading...</a>

title: Colombia’s new president Abelardo de la Espriella announces immigration crackdown
description: <p>Far-right leader echoes ally Donald Trump and says operations to ‘track down illegal immigrants’ should begin this week, amid earthquake aftermath</p><p>Colombia’s far-right president, Abelardo de la Espriella, has announced a crackdown on immigrants, ordering authorities to detain and deport people who are in the country irregularly or have committed crimes.</p><p>In office for just over two weeks, the millionaire former lawyer made the announcement on Sunday as the country continued to grapple with the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/11/colombia-earthquake-dead-amid-hunt-for-survivors">aftermath of a 7.4-magnitude earthquake</a> on 10 August that killed more than 300 people and destroyed more than 30,000 homes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/25/colombia-immigration-crackdown-president-abelardo-de-la-espriella">Continue reading...</a>

title: US strikes a vessel in the eastern Pacific, killing 2 people in first attack in months
description: <p>US Southern Command has struck another vessel in the eastern Pacific, killing two accused of trafficking drugs</p><p>The US military has launched a deadly strike on a vessel in the Pacific Ocean, killing two people accused of drug trafficking.</p><p>On Monday, US Southern Command (SouthCom) <a href="https://x.com/Southcom/status/2091757856018104599?s=20">announced</a> it “executed a lethal kinetic strike on a low-profile vessel operating along established narco-trafficking routes in the Eastern Pacific”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/24/vessel-strike-eastern-pacific">Continue reading...</a>

title: Typhoon Narra: record flood waters submerge homes and force mass evacuations in China
description: <p>Heavy rain expected in parts of Vietnam and southern ‌China, as another storm system, Typhoon Saudel, heads for Japan and Taiwan</p><p>Widespread flooding triggered by Typhoon Narra has submerged homes and forced mass evacuations in southern China, as another storm system tracked towards Japan and Taiwan.</p><p>Authorities in Chongzuo, in China’s Guangxi region – famous for its giant waterfalls and karst limestone mountains – on Tuesday evacuated more than 15,000 people after water ⁠levels surpassed a record high set in 2008.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/26/typhoon-narra-floods-evacuations-china">Continue reading...</a>

title: Taiwan charges nine people for smuggling ‘high-end’ AI servers to China
description: <p>Among those charged are two Super Micro employees and one from Nvidia, marking another flashpoint in US-China AI rivalry</p><p>Taiwanese prosecutors charged nine people Monday, including one from Nvidia and two from Super Micro, for illegally exporting “high-end AI servers” to mainland China, adding another wave of turbulence in the AI ​​rivalry between China and the United States.</p><p>Prosecutors said the servers involved were graphics processing units known as “B300,” which have been banned from sale to China.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/aug/25/taiwan-china-ai-smugglers">Continue reading...</a>

title: China denounces US threat of sanctions over trade with Iran
description: <p>Beijing says it will take ‘all necessary measures’ to protect its interests as US steps up efforts to isolate Tehran</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/25/trump-us-economic-sanctions-china-biggest-buyer-iran-oil">Explainer: could US sanctions threaten China-Iran ties?</a></p></li></ul><p>China has denounced the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/24/us-severe-sanctions-economic-ties-iran">threat of US sanctions for its trade with Iran</a>, saying any such measures would be illegal, and warned it would take “all necessary measures” to protect its national interests.</p><p>Beijing’s rejection of the US threat of secondary sanctions for any country or entity continuing to trade with Tehran had been predicted. China buys an estimated 80% of Iran’s oil exports and has defied previous US efforts to limit the flow of revenue to the Tehran regime.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/25/china-us-sanctions-iran-oil">Continue reading...</a>

title: Artist known for sculptures of Mao Zedong jailed for slandering ‘heroes and martyrs’
description: <p>Gao Zhen sentenced to three years in prison after already spending two years in detention</p><p>Gao Zhen, a prominent Chinese artist known for provocative sculptures of the former leader Mao Zedong, has been sentenced to three years in prison after being found guilty of slandering China’s “heroes and martyrs”. The sentencing came two years after he was detained while visiting the country with his family, according to his wife and human rights groups.</p><p>The <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/31/dissident-artist-gao-zhen-tried-china-satirical-mao-sculptures-rights-group">case has attracted international condemnation</a>, largely because the artworks at the centre of the case were created more than 10 years before China created the law under which Gao was charged.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/25/artist-gao-zhen-sculptures-mao-zedong-jailed-china">Continue reading...</a>

description: <p>Follow updates live</p><ul><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">breaking news email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p><strong>Angela Jackson,</strong> the commissioner of the Productivity Commission, said the body stands by the interim report into the GST, which found the deal with Western Australia to be a costly mistake that should be reversed.</p><p>Jackson spoke to RN this morning after WA premier <strong>Roger Cook</strong> said “east coast clowns” didn’t understand the state and any changes would “rip $6bn out of the Western Australia economy”.</p><p>We are aiming, of course, to inform public policy debate, which can often get heated. description: <p>Protests and petitions planned amid growing concerns over impact of climate crisis on numbers of Alpine rodent</p><p>Animal rights campaigners are gearing up for protests and petitions aimed at persuading the French government to ban the hunting of Alpine marmots.</p><p>Open season on the rodents, members of the squirrel and groundhog family, begins in September, a few weeks before they go into a long winter hibernation.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/26/call-ban-marmot-hunting-france-climate-crisis">Continue reading...</a>

title: Man on trial for Daphne Caruana Galizia murder claims he was framed
description: <p>Yorgen Fenech tells jury he had nothing to do with killing and alleges top adviser to Malta’s then PM was instigator</p><p>A businessman on trial for the murder of the journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia has spoken about the charges for the first time in court since his arrest seven years ago, telling the jury he was framed by police and had nothing to do with the killing.</p><p>During four days of questioning by defence and the prosecution lawyers, Yorgen Fenech, 44, accused the most senior adviser to Malta’s prime minister of giving the go-ahead for the murder.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/26/yorgen-fenech-trial-daphne-caruana-galizia-claims-framed">Continue reading...</a>

title: FBI raided Spanish vacation rental of wealthy leftwing funder James ‘Fergie’ Chambers after his arrest
description: <p>Lawyer Baltasar Garzón, representing Chambers, said case against his client is ‘very strange’ as US requests extradition</p><p>FBI agents raided the Ibiza, Spain, vacation rental of 41-year-old James “Fergie” Chambers, a US citizen and wealthy donor to leftwing and humanitarian projects worldwide, in the days following his arrest last month, the Guardian has learned.</p><p><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltasar_Garz%C3%B3n">Baltasar Garzón,</a> a human rights lawyer representing Chambers, revealed the details in an exclusive interview. Chambers is wanted for extradition by the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/trump-administration">Trump administration</a> for alleged financial support of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/hamas">Hamas</a>, as well as other charges.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/25/fbi-raid-james-fergie-cox-vacation-rental">Continue reading...</a>

title: CIA director John Ratcliffe reportedly on Moscow visit
description: <p>Unannounced trip reported by US media is said to be Ratcliffe’s first known visit to Russia as CIA chief</p><p>The CIA director, John Ratcliffe, has made an unannounced visit to Moscow, US media reported, after flight data showed an American military aircraft flew to the Russian capital, where a US diplomatic motorcade was later spotted.</p><p>CBS News quoted sources familiar with the situation as confirming Ratcliffe’s trip, saying it was his first known visit to Russia as CIA chief. title: Iran seeks to criminalise all contact with foreign media in latest ‘chilling’ crackdown
description: <p>As photojournalist sentenced to 15 years, rights groups warn law would turn civic engagement into security crime</p><p>Iran has taken the first step towards criminalising contact with foreign media, in a move human rights groups have said attempts to “sever the entire Iranian society from the rest of the world”.</p><p>For journalists, researchers and even ordinary citizens, the proposed law being discussed by Iranian lawmakers this month could make speaking to international audiences and groups a potential criminal act and restrict coverage of events such as <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/ng-interactive/2026/feb/15/new-photos-give-glimpse-inside-irans-bloody-crackdown-on-anti-government-protests">January’s mass anti-regime protests</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/aug/26/iran-criminalises-contact-foreign-media-human-rights-crackdown">Continue reading...</a>

title: Iran faces strait of Hormuz paradox as strategic value of chokehold erodes
description: <p>Internal calls to end war get louder as Gulf neighbours plan alternative pipelines to cut reliance on waterway</p><p>Is the strait of Hormuz, recently cited by the office of the Iranian supreme leader as “the pillar of Iran’s new security order”, and as transformative as possessing a nuclear weapon, in reality becoming a fast-diminishing asset, leaving Iran increasingly vulnerable to the new planned US wave of economic sanctions?</p><p>It is the key debate that is raging inside Iran, with many different conclusions being drawn for Tehran’s negotiating strategy. title: Iran-linked hackers blamed for cyber-attack that shut down UK power plant

title: Iran’s foreign minister calls threat of new US economic sanctions ‘desperate’
description: <p>Abbas Araghchi says country is unbowed but president Masoud Pezeshkian admits its people face ‘many problems’</p><p>Iran’s foreign minister has dismissed the threat of a fresh round of US economic sanctions as a “desperate” ploy, even as its president acknowledged that the Iranian people are facing “many problems” amid Washington’s efforts to isolate and debilitate the country’s economy.</p><p>Last week, Donald Trump announced a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/20/trump-threatens-crush-iran-economy-war-hormuz">new campaign to increase the pressure on the Iranian economy</a>, calling it “the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country”. title: At least 14 newborn babies die in fire at Pakistan hospital’s maternity ward
description: <p>Authorities at biggest state hospital in Islamabad say 15 babies were in the ward when fire broke out</p><p>At least 14 newborn babies have died in a fire that broke out in the maternity ward at one of Pakistan’s most prominent state hospitals.</p><p>The blaze began in the early hours of Wednesday and engulfed the ward at Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences, the biggest state hospital in Islamabad.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/26/newborn-babies-die-fire-pakistan-hospital-maternity-ward">Continue reading...</a>

title: The whitewashing of the Green India Mission forest expansion project
description: <p>The flagship environmental initiative has achieved ‘negligible’ results. Why so little progress, and what are the risks as the planet gets hotter? Plus, fusion dance pioneer Usha Jey</p><p><strong>• </strong><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jul/30/sign-up-for-this-is-india-our-free-weekly-newsletter-on-life-in-the-subcontinent"><strong>Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here</strong></a></p><p>India set out to expand its forested areas a decade ago. Last week, however, we learned that the forest cover programme had barely taken root when the <a href="https://cag.gov.in/cen/mumbai/en/audit-report/details/126059">government’s auditors released their findings</a> of the flagship Green India Mission. The shortfall of 97.57% from India’s initial pledge in 2014 was stark enough to alarm the government’s own auditor, who described the progress as “negligible”.</p><p>Yet if you ask the government about forest cover, you’ll get a far greener picture.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/24/the-whitewashing-of-the-green-indian-mission">Continue reading...</a>

title: Jailed ex-Pakistan PM Imran Khan allowed brief hospital visit after uproar over health
description:
<p>Supreme court ordered transfer of ex-leader whose health is reportedly deteriorating, but he was returned to prison several hours later</p><p><br>
 Pakistan’s jailed former prime minister <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/imran-khan">Imran Khan</a> was briefly taken to a hospital in the country’s capital on supreme court orders after weeks of uproar about his deteriorating health.</p><p>Khan, 73, was transferred to the hospital in the early hours of Friday, but then moved back to Adiala prison in Rawalpindi after a ⁠few hours, a spokesperson for his party said on Friday.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/20/imran-khan-hospital-pakistan">Continue reading...</a>

title: Taliban threaten former Afghan police worker after MoD leak reveals identity
description: <p>UK has refused resettlement application despite ‘years of loyal service’ that have resulted in ‘constant fear’ of reprisals</p><p>A man has received threats from the Taliban after his work for the Afghan police was revealed by a Ministry of Defence leak and the UK refused his application for resettlement.</p><p>Hamid* worked for the Afghan national police special unit and received certificates for his work signed by senior British figures praising his “dedication, unparalleled service and leadership”. His details were also included in an <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2025/jul/15/afghan-resettlement-scheme-secret-superinjunction-explainer">accidental 2022 leak</a> by an MoD official that identified 18,700 Afghans who had worked with or for the British government.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/16/taliban-threaten-former-afghan-police-worker-after-mod-leak-reveals-identity">Continue reading...</a>

title: Concerns grow over increased global ties with Taliban in Afghanistan
description: <p>Campaigners fear deeper diplomatic contacts are undermining demands for improvements in human rights </p><p>The Taliban in Afghanistan have launched a diplomatic effort to end their isolation as major regional and international powers show a readiness to engage more closely with the repressive regime despite its systematic human rights abuses.</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/aug/04/five-years-taliban-rule-afghan-women-and-girls-need-our-help">Five years after the Taliban took power</a>, an increasing number of countries are renewing ties or scaling up diplomatic contacts with the hardline Islamists, who seized power in Kabul in 2021 after 20 years of brutal insurgent warfare.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/15/concern-grow-global-ties-taliban-afghanistan-human-rights">Continue reading...</a>

title: Burnham announces plan for 10,000 work experience placements for young people – UK politics live
description: <p>Prime minister spoke to press while on visit to a Sainsbury’s supermarket this morning</p><p><strong>Burnham</strong> was asked by reporters whether he was a <strong>Dolly Parton</strong> fan, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/aug/25/dolly-parton-dead-age-80-live">as tributes pour in for the country music legend</a> who died yesterday at the age of 80.</p><p>The prime minister said:</p><p>“I was a huge fan of what Dolly did around literacy around the world. I was culture secretary when her libraries were first coming through and the books that went into communities across Britain, you know, what a legacy to leave.</p><p>And it was so moving to hear about her dad and how that experience made her want to give back so much. So, yeah, she leaves that legacy as well as obviously great music that people will treasure for ever.”</p><p>It’s why, within days of taking office, I announced that we would remove VAT off electricity bills to give people that little bit of help.</p><p>That kicks in from October.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/aug/26/andy-burnham-labour-neets-youth-unemployment-work-placements-ofgem-energy-bills-reform-jenrick-latest-news-updates">Continue reading...</a>

title: London rollout of robotaxis delayed amid lack of guidance for firms to follow
description: <p>Uber and Wayve had said they would start trips ‘later this summer’ but launch now looks unlikely this year</p><p>The rollout of robotaxis on the streets of London is unlikely to happen this year, as regulatory and technical hurdles push back the ambitious schedule set out by the UK government.</p><p>Only weeks ago Uber and London-based Wayve were granted the first minicab licences in the capital to allow them to offer self-driving taxi rides to paying customers – but with a human safety driver in place, for now – and said they would start trips <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/aug/05/self-driving-taxis-approved-london-summer-2026-wayve-uber">“later this summer” before a full public launch</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/aug/26/london-rollout-robotaxis-delayed-uber-wayve">Continue reading...</a>

title: Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and nitrous oxide possession
description: <ul><li><p>Former England forward crashed on M3 in late May</p></li><li><p>Sterling is also accused of failing to provide a specimen</p></li></ul><p>The former England forward Raheem Sterling has been charged with dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/30/raheem-sterling-suffered-immeasurable-psychological-strain-close-source-says">a crash involving a Lamborghini</a> on the motorway, police have said.</p><p>Hampshire and Isle of Wight constabulary said the charges followed a single-vehicle collision on the M3 southbound, near Minley interchange, on 28 May. The 31-year-old is accused of dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/aug/26/raheem-sterling-charged-with-dangerous-driving-and-nitrous-oxide-possession">Continue reading...</a>

title: Heatwaves show UK must do more to promote cycling and walking, campaigners say
description: <p>Civil society groups argue climate crisis means transport sector needs to urgently reduce its carbon emissions</p><p>Dozens of civil society groups have demanded the UK government do more to promote cycling and walking, after this summer’s extreme heat exposed the desperate need to decarbonise transport.</p><p>This summer’s heatwaves and wildfires were “immediate, real-world manifestations of the climate emergency”, the groups said, making reform of transport – responsible for more carbon emissions than any other sector in the UK – an urgent priority.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/aug/26/heatwaves-uk-promote-cycling-walking">Continue reading...</a>

title: Britons face highest price cap in three years as energy bills rise 4% from October
description: <p>Households in Great Britain will pay equivalent of £1,723 a year, prompting calls for more support</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/nils-pratley-on-finance/2026/aug/26/labour-energy-bills-crisis-political-honesty-essential">Nils Pratley: Labour’s energy bills crisis is getting worse. Political honesty is essential</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/aug/26/uk-households-4-rise-energy-bills-average-1723-october-live-updates">Business live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Millions of households in Great Britain will face the highest energy charges in three years this winter after months of soaring market prices caused the government’s price cap to rise for a second time in three months.</p><p>Gas and electricity prices will rise by 4% from October under the new cap, months after <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/money/2026/may/27/energy-price-cap-great-britain-rise-july-gas-electricity-iran-war">climbing 13%</a> at the start of July to take account of soaring global energy market prices caused by the war on Iran.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/money/2026/aug/26/energy-price-cap-great-britain-to-rise-from-october">Continue reading...</a>

description: <p>Legendary country singer died surrounded by loved ones after being diagnosed with cancer, her team says; Beyoncé, Taylor Swift and Dionne Warwick lead tributes</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/aug/25/dolly-parton-country-singer-dead">Dolly Parton dies aged 80</a> </p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/aug/25/dolly-parton-death-celebrity-reactions">Celebrity tributes</a> </p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/music/gallery/2026/aug/25/dolly-parton-life-in-pictures">A life in pictures</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/aug/25/dolly-parton-country-music-career">Parton’s peerless career turned country music cliches inside out</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/aug/25/share-your-tributes-and-memories-of-dolly-parton">Share your tributes and memories of Dolly Parton</a></p></li></ul><p>Our picture editors have collated <strong>Dolly Parton</strong>’s life in pictures:</p><p>In the UK, top radio presenter Jo Whiley introduced her BBC Radio 2 evening show by playing <strong>I Will Always Love You</strong>, <strong>Jolene</strong> and <strong>9 to 5</strong> in tribute to <strong>Dolly Parton</strong> after her death was announced in the 7pm news headlines.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/aug/25/dolly-parton-dead-age-80-live">Continue reading...</a>

title: Celebrity tributes pour in for Dolly Parton: ‘a gift to the world’
description: <p>Lily Tomlin, Taylor Swift, Beyoncé, Céline Dion and Oprah Winfrey are among those remembering the queen of country <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/aug/25/dolly-parton-country-singer-dead">after she died aged 80</a></p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/aug/25/dolly-parton-country-music-career">Alexis Petridis on Dolly Parton’s peerless career that turned country music cliches inside out</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/music/gallery/2026/aug/25/dolly-parton-life-in-pictures">Dolly Parton – a life in pictures</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/aug/25/dolly-parton-dead-age-80-live">Country music legend Dolly Parton dies aged 80 – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Tributes have poured in for <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/music/dolly-parton">Dolly Parton</a>, the country singer, songwriter and actor, after her death aged 80.</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/aug/25/dolly-parton-country-singer-dead">News of her death</a> was shared by her nephew <a href="https://x.com/DollyParton/status/2092309743981228273">on social media</a>. “Dolly has lived in the light and is in the arms of Jesus,” he said.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/aug/25/dolly-parton-death-celebrity-reactions">Continue reading...</a>

title: Wednesday briefing: How Canada has turned a trade dispute into a defence of its sovereignty
description: <p>In today’s newsletter: A collapsing trade deal has united Canadians more than ever, in an existential confrontation with the US president</p><p></p><p>Good morning. When the Guardian asked Canadian readers whether they planned to boycott US products after dramatic escalations in the ongoing DC/Ottawa trade war, we received more than 2,000 responses within 12 hours.</p><p>This inundation is perhaps evidence of the existential crisis many Canadians feel they now face, something often lost in the granular reporting of trade negotiations: this is about so much more than the price of lumber.</p><p><em><strong>US news </strong></em>| Dolly Parton, one of the greatest singer-songwriters in country music who was also much cherished for her philanthropy, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/aug/25/dolly-parton-country-singer-dead">has died aged 80</a>.</p><p><em><strong>UK news </strong></em>| UK citizens <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/aug/25/uk-to-warn-citizens-to-stock-up-on-food-amid-threat-from-climate-crisis-and-hostile-states">will be told to stock up on tinned food </a>and take steps to ensure they are prepared for national emergencies as part of a new government campaign to improve the nation’s resilience.</p><p><em><strong>UK politics </strong></em>| Andy Burnham <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/aug/25/andy-burnham-electoral-reform-first-past-the-post">will face an immediate test</a> of his backing for electoral reform in his first week in parliament as prime minister, with almost 100 Labour MPs supporting a bid for a new national commission.</p><p><em><strong>Ukraine </strong></em>| A man from South Yorkshire is believed to be the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/aug/25/yorkshireman-briton-die-fighting-russia-ukraine">first British citizen to die</a> fighting for Russia in its war against Ukraine.</p><p><em><strong>Climate crisis </strong></em>| The carbon emissions from just two planned datacentres in England will <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/aug/25/planned-datacentres-carbon-emissions-uk-exxonmobil">exceed all of the fossil fuel company ExxonMobil’s UK emissions</a>, analysis has revealed.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/26/wednesday-briefing-how-canada-has-turned-a-trade-dispute-into-a-defence-of-its-sovereignty">Continue reading...</a>

title: Two Dan Sullivans to appear on Alaska’s US Senate ballot in November’s midterm elections
description: <p>The incumbent senator  Dan S Sullivan has condemned ex-school teacher Dan J Sullivan, claiming he is running at the behest of Democrats to confuse supporters</p><p>Republican senator Dan S Sullivan will be joined on the November ballot in Alaska by a challenger with a nearly identical name from the same party, election officials confirmed on Tuesday, adding a twist to what is expected to be one of the most hotly contested races of the midterms.</p><p>The Republican senator is running for a third term <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/19/alaska-senate-primary-results">against Democrat Mary Peltola</a>, a former US House representative whom polls show is neck-and-neck with him in a state that hasn’t sent a Democrat to the Senate since 2008.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/26/alaska-dan-sullivan-senate">Continue reading...</a>
