title: South-Africa kingpin and the corruption commission
description: In tonight's programme, a three-day testimony of an alleged underworld kingpin exposed how deep the link between alleged criminals and high profile police officers is in South Africa. Also, in Tunisia grieving families lay their lost youth, all victims of a boat that went down in the Mediterranean Sea over the weekend. And finally in an era of mass production and electric machines, a young Kenyan fashion designer is taking a slower approach.

title: Navigation, jurisdiction, costs: Iran, Oman attempt to hammer out Hormuz deal
description: Iran and Oman are holding talks to try to reach an interim agreement for a controlled resumption of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. The two countries have discussed a framework for a “temporary corridor” for shipping, according to a joint statement by the Iranian and Omani foreign ministries. But the plan faces several hurdles.

title: Tim Curry, star of 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show' and 'It', dies at 80
description: Tim Curry, the British character actor who created a gallery of flamboyant villains for stage and screen, most famously Dr. Frank-N-Furter in the 1975 cult classic "The Rocky Horror Picture Show", has died at the age of 80, his manager said on Wednesday.

title: Exclusive: French astronaut Sophie Adenot recounts her ‘miracle’ mission from orbiting ISS
description: In an exclusive interview with FRANCE 24 and RFI from the International Space Station, French astronaut Sophie Adenot hailed a "mission accomplished" after two spacewalks to replace a faulty antenna and called the operation "a miracle", given the mechanical setbacks. She also described the "blatant" signs of climate change she has seen from orbit.

title: Space: Sophie Adenot recounts her two spacewalks
description:
🇫🇷 👩‍🚀 Sophie Adenot, the first French woman to conduct a spacewalk and the second female French astronaut to go to space, gave an exclusive interview to #FRANCE24 and #RFI from the International Space Station.
 
In conversation with our journalists, she reflected on the feeling of leaping into the vast unknown of space for the first time.

title: Syria: Why is the dissolution of the Kurdish forces significant?
description: The Syrian Kurdish Forces announced their dissolution on August 25, in what is considered a significant step for Syria. FRANCE 24's Andrew Hilliar tells us why.

title: Dolly Parton: Buckingham Palace guards play musical tribute
description: Britain’s royal family posted a video on social media Wednesday of the band of the Buckingham Palace guards playing Dolly Parton’s “9 to 5”, in tribute to the American country music legend who passed away Tuesday aged 80.

title: ‘Shockwaves throughout the country’ following ‘gruesome’ killings in Haitian mountain retreat
description: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome journalist Harold Isaac on the ground in Haiti's capital, Port-au-Prince. He says what we are witnessing in Haiti is not simply another episode of gang violence, but a profound challenge to the authority of the state at a moment when the country is attempting to return to electoral politics. With armed groups controlling roughly 80 percent of Port-au-Prince, the capital is effectively under siege, while the circulation of people, goods and services increasingly requires some form of negotiation with gang power. The attack in Kenscoff is especially significant because of its proximity to some of the country’s most affluent areas. This as authorities seek to organize Haiti’s first elections in a decade, against a backdrop of arms smuggling, institutional fragility and an unresolved political transition.

title: Russia: CIA director visits Moscow
description: CIA director John Ratcliffe held talks with Russian intelligence services in Moscow, the Kremlin confirmed Wednesday, the first know visit by a US spy chief to the Russian capital since 2021. It is not known what Ratcliffe discussed with his Russian counterparts, but the talks come as ‌the war in Ukraine is escalating and as ⁠efforts to reach a lasting peace between the US and Iran have stalled.

title: Tornado wreaks havoc in village in southwestern France
description: A tornado swept through a village in the Aude ​region of southwestern France late on Monday, destroying homes and injuring dozens, authorities said, describing it as a rare and traumatic event. Around 300 of the 500 houses in the ​village of ‌Pomas have been damaged, officials said, adding that 100 of ⁠the damaged ones may no longer be safe to live in.

title: Hundreds missing in Nepal catastrophic flash floods
description: Massive flash floods in Nepal on Wednesday killed at least 22 people and left hundreds of tourists, workers and others missing after sweeping through communities and bringing travel in parts of the Himalayan country to a halt. China's government across the northern border also launched search and rescue efforts, with major casualties in the border area of Gyirong, state broadcaster CCTV reported. No toll was immediately reported.

title: From tariffs to French: Trump’s trade war with Canada takes a cultural turn
description: A trade war between Canada and the United States is escalating. Canada has announced retaliatory tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on about $20 billion worth of American goods, after new 50% US tariffs on Canadian products took effect Saturday. But the tit-for-tat over goods has also taken on a cultural and linguistic dimension.

title: Dolly Parton, queen of country music, dies at 80
description: Dolly Parton was around six when she wrote her first song: "Little Tiny Tasseltop," an ⁠ode to her corncob doll with ​corn-silk hair. Her mother stored it preciously in a shoebox. Parton never stopped making music after that. The irrepressible country music singer, songwriter and actress whose charisma, heartfelt lyrics and ​business acumen captured the public's imagination for nearly six decades, died on Tuesday aged 80, her family said in a statement.

title: 'Major casualties': Devastating floods wash away villages on Nepal-Tibet border
description: Massive flooding near the border with Tibet killed dozens in Nepal on Wednesday. Hundreds of people were still out of contact hours after the disaster hit. A torrent of mud and debris burst from the banks of a river between China and Nepal, burying buildings and triggering a frantic search for survivors. FRANCE 24's Sarah Jacob reports from New Delhi, India.

title: Turkey says dissolution of Kurdish-led group crucial for Syrian stability
description: Turkey on Wednesday said the dissolution of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) marked a key step towards strengthening state authority and achieving lasting stability in Syria. Turkey has long regarded the SDF as an extension of the outlawed Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), which waged an insurgency against the Turkish state for decades. FRANCE 24's Jasper Mortimer reports from Ankara, Turkey.

title: Gang attack in Haiti: Anger mounts over police failures
description: At least 47 people were killed and more than 50 others kidnapped after armed men attacked a once-peaceful community near Haiti’s capital earlier this week, the United Nations said Tuesday. It is believed to be one of the largest mass kidnappings in Haiti in recent years, and one gang leader is threatening to kill the hostages if authorities kill any gang members as they try to secure the community nestled in the hills above Port-au-Prince. Sunday’s attack on Kenscoff pierced the belief that security in the troubled Caribbean country was improving. Journalist Harold Isaac reports from Port-au-Prince, Haiti.

title: 'In Ceuta, they are eating the cats': Fake images and a persistent rumour
description: Cats “massacred” in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta? Three weeks after thousands of migrants crossed the border into Ceuta, Spanish websites and social media users are claiming that the migrants who have stayed are killing cats. But all of the dead cat photos that have been shared so far are either fake or have been taken out of context. Our team spoke to a local cat rescue organisation, which also confirmed that this is a rumour.

title: South African police arrest two Thai men for allegedly smuggling parrot eggs
description: <p>Bird eggs intercepted in homemade incubators at Johannesburg airport as officials try to halt wildlife trafficking</p><p>South African police have arrested two Thai nationals in separate incidents for allegedly attempting to smuggle endangered parrot eggs out of the country as authorities try to stem the tide of wildlife trafficking.</p><p>A 50-year-old Thai national was arrested at OR Tambo international airport in Johannesburg on 20 August, carrying 50 bird eggs in a homemade incubator in a hand-luggage bag, South Africa’s environment ministry said in a <a href="https://www.dffe.gov.za/mediarelease/arrest_allegedwildlifetrafficker">statement</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/26/south-african-police-arrest-two-thai-men-smuggling-parrot-eggs">Continue reading...</a>

title: How to lose Trump’s trade war: test Canada’s resolve with threats to hockey sticks
description: <p>The US president expected Ottawa to bow to tariff demands, but Canada is striking back – and it could cost Americans</p><ul><li><p><strong>This was originally published in This Week in Trumpland. </strong><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2024/apr/25/election-newsletter-sign-up-stakes"><strong>Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Wednesday</strong></a></p></li></ul><p>Earlier this year, a survey found that <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/canada">Canada</a>, along with <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/switzerland">Switzerland</a>, was <a href="https://www.visualcapitalist.com/ranked-worlds-most-and-least-liked-countries/">the best-liked country</a> in the world. We all know this kind of polling is about as scientific as a high school popularity contest, but at least anecdotally, Canadians have a reputation for being friendly and welcoming, respectful and polite. Many people would find it difficult to dislike Canadians.</p><p>But not Donald Trump, who in a “hold my beer” moment this week demonstrated that he, at least, finds it easy to resent Canadians. The US president called the country “difficult and unreasonable”, and in a particularly hysterical moment, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/aug/25/donald-trump-tariffs-canada-midterms-primary-south-carolina-iran-ukraine-voting-rights-latest-news-updates?page=with%3Ablock-6a8d78948f08c9649271ddc9#block-6a8d78948f08c9649271ddc9">threatened to rename a lake</a>, after trade talks collapsed.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/26/trump-canada-trade-war">Continue reading...</a>

title: Girl, 13, among missing British citizens after flash flood in Nepal
description: <p>More than 400 travellers are said to be missing after flood on Tibet border, including 33 Britons</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/aug/26/nepal-tibet-himalayas-flash-floods-missing-foreign-tourists-latest-news-updates">Flash floods on Nepal-Tibet border – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Thirty-three British citizens including a 13-year-old girl are among more than 400 travellers missing after a flash flood on the Nepal-Tibet border, according to Nepal’s tourism board.</p><p>The sudden flood happened on the Tibetan side of the Bhote Koshi River at about 8.30am local time on Wednesday. The 33 UK citizens are among at least 341 foreign nationals unaccounted for.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/26/missing-british-citizens-flash-flood-nepal">Continue reading...</a>

title: ‘Escape wizard’ who has broken out of four prisons is arrested in Spain
description: <p>Albanian criminal has cut bars, descended sheets and even used human pyramid in escapes in Italy and Belgium</p><p>Police in Spain have arrested a dangerous Albanian criminal nicknamed the “escape wizard” who has managed to break out of four jails in Italy and Belgium by sawing through bars, clambering down knotted sheets and even using a human pyramid to breach prison walls.</p><p>The fugitive, who has not been officially named, was arrested after officers from the Policía Nacional force discovered he was living in the north-eastern Spanish city of Tarragona. He was the subject of a European arrest warrant issued by the Italian authorities.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/26/escape-wizard-albanian-fugitive-toma-taulant-arrested-spain-after-breaking-out-of-four-jails">Continue reading...</a>

description: <p>Andy Burnham stops short of pledging further help as gas and electricity prices due to increase by 4% in October</p><p>Households are unlikely to receive further energy bills support before the October price cap, though more targeted measures could be looked at if there is a further shock in January, government sources said.</p><p>Gas and electricity prices will rise by 4% from October <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/money/2026/aug/26/energy-price-cap-great-britain-to-rise-from-october">under the new cap</a>. The government has already removed VAT from domestic electricity bills to save average households £45 a year, a move announced in Andy Burnham’s first week in office.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/aug/26/energy-bills-support-price-cap-rise-andy-burnham">Continue reading...</a>

title: ‘Work is good for you’: how UK scheme could help tackle youth mental health crisis
description: <p>Paid employment can boost confidence and wellbeing, says Pat McFadden as jobs guarantee scheme gets under way</p><p>Work must be “part of the answer” to the mental health crisis among young people, the work and pensions secretary, Pat McFadden, has said as he met some of the first beneficiaries of Labour’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/jun/28/employers-great-britain-3000-for-every-long-term-unemployed-young-person-they-hire">youth jobs guarantee scheme</a>.</p><p>He was speaking on a visit to Boots’s headquarters in Nottingham on Wednesday, where several 18- to 21-year-olds were taken on under the job guarantee – with their wages paid by the taxpayer for six months.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/aug/26/work-good-for-you-jobs-guarantee-youth-mental-health-crisis-pat-mcfadden">Continue reading...</a>

title: Plug-in balcony solar panels to go on sale in UK for first time
description: <p>DIY system will be stocked by big retailers, starting with Argos, enabling more homes to lower bills by generating own electricity</p><p>Plug-in solar panels will go on sale in the UK for the first time from Thursday, allowing households unable to use rooftop panels to also generate their own cheap electricity.</p><p>Households across the country will be able to join the millions across mainland Europe who generate their own renewable electricity using “balcony solar panels”, which will be stocked by some of the UK’s biggest retailers.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/aug/26/plug-in-balcony-solar-panels-to-go-on-sale-in-uk-for-first-time">Continue reading...</a>

title: Burnham drops support for political funding cap aimed at curbing mega-donors
description: <p>PM said he would set bar at £500k, but trade unions say funding reforms could undermine their ability to donate to Labour</p><p>Andy Burnham has dropped his support for capping political donations, causing anger among activists and Labour MPs who have long campaigned for change to the way parties are funded.</p><p>The prime minister has decided not to back amendments to the elections bill, which would cap the amount a person or an organisation can give in a single donation, according to government sources.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/aug/26/burnham-political-donations-influence-elections-bill">Continue reading...</a>

title: Wes Streeting describes ‘unbelievable volume’ of homophobic abuse since becoming defence secretary
description: <p>Streeting says role is chance to show strength and challenge stereotype that ‘persists in dark corners of internet’</p><p>Wes Streeting has described receiving a mass of homophobic abuse since he was made defence secretary last month, while also saying his appointment had been welcomed by some in the Ministry of Defence (MoD) as a sign of change.</p><p>Until 2000, gay men and lesbian women were banned from serving in the UK military, with about 200-plus personnel thrown out of the forces each year due to their sexuality – an estimate, as proper records were not kept.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/aug/26/wes-streeting-homophobic-abuse-uk-defence-secretary">Continue reading...</a>

title: Final witness in Lindsay Clancy trial says he doesn’t believe she heard a voice during killings
description: <p>FBI psychiatrist Gregory Saathoff says he has treated only two women with postpartum psychosis, both decades earlier</p><p>Testimony finished in the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/22/lindsay-clancy-trial-what-happened-this-week">Lindsay Clancy trial</a> on Wednesday, as a final witness for the prosecution laid out that he believed the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/massachusetts">Massachusetts</a> mother knew right from wrong when she took the lives of her three young children before attempting to commit suicide in 2023.</p><p>Closing arguments are expected to begin on Thursday. The jury will then start deliberating.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/26/lindsay-clancy-trial-fbi-psychiatrist-final-witness">Continue reading...</a>

title: FDA gives expedited approval to new groundbreaking pancreatic cancer drug
description: <p>FDA officials approve first-of-a-kind pill called daraxonrasib to fight one of the deadliest types of cancer</p><p>The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a groundbreaking new drug for the most common form of pancreatic cancer, offering US patients a more effective treatment against one of the deadliest types of the disease.</p><p>FDA officials gave expedited approval to the first-of-a-kind pill, called daraxonrasib, that blocks a mutated protein which fuels tumor growth in more than 90% of pancreatic cancer cases. It’s an approach that has eluded drugmakers for decades.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/26/fda-approves-new-pancreatic-cancer-drug">Continue reading...</a>

title: Texas law banning drag shows where children may be present struck down again
description: <p>‘This is a profoundly flawed decision that endangers our children and is an affront to Texas values,’ Ken Paxton says</p><p>A federal judge has, for a second time, struck down a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/texas">Texas</a> state law banning drag performances in settings where children may be present.</p><p>In a ruling issued on Tuesday, US district judge David Hittner said Texas cannot enforce its drag show ban. He said that the measure improperly restricts speech and violates the first amendment of the US constitution.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/26/texas-drag-performance-ban-fails">Continue reading...</a>
